questions.q: What does OLTP stand for, and what is it optimized for?
options: Online Transaction Processing — many small, fast individual reads and writes
Online Table Persistence — permanent storage of every table
Offline Transaction Processing — batch jobs run overnight only
Online Table Partitioning — splitting large tables automatically
questions.explain: OLTP systems handle high volumes of small, individual transactions like placing one order or updating one address.

questions.q: What does OLAP stand for, and what is it optimized for?
options: Online Analytical Processing — big, aggregate queries across millions of historical rows
Online Application Protocol — network communication between servers
Offline Analytical Processing — analysis that only runs when disconnected
Online Archive Protection — backing up historical data
questions.explain: OLAP systems are read-heavy and built for fast aggregation across huge volumes of historical data.

questions.q: Why does an OLTP system benefit from the normalization rules in Chapter 11?
options: It updates data constantly, and normalization prevents the same fact from going stale in two different places at once
Normalization makes OLTP queries slower on purpose
OLTP systems never need to update data after it's inserted
Normalization is required by SQL Server for all OLTP databases
questions.explain: Frequent updates mean duplicated facts risk drifting out of sync — normalization directly addresses that risk.

questions.q: Why is an OLAP system usually denormalized on purpose?
options: Fewer joins means faster aggregate queries across huge volumes of data
Denormalization is required by law for reporting systems
OLAP systems cannot use foreign keys at all
It's a side effect with no real benefit
questions.explain: Since OLAP is read-heavy and rarely updated, the update-consistency risk normalization solves matters far less than query speed.

questions.q: Which real database pair on the student's server demonstrates OLTP vs. OLAP?
options: AdventureWorks2012 (OLTP) and AdventureWorksDW2014 (OLAP)
AdventureWorks2012 and Northwind, both OLTP
AdventureWorksDW2014 used for both OLTP and OLAP labs
There is no such example — this is only a theoretical distinction
questions.explain: AdventureWorksDW2014 restructures the same company's data into a denormalized warehouse shape for analysis.
